department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering
summary: A funded PhD investigating how concrete chemically and mechanically degrades over time, to improve the durability and lifespan of concrete infrastructure.
title: Unravelling the chemo-mechanical degradation of concrete

department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering
summary: A funded PhD studying how extreme weather destabilises coastal cliffs, to safeguard the resilience of geo-infrastructure under climate change.
title: The investigation of coastal cliff instability due to extreme weather conditions

department: Department of Engineering Science
summary: A 3.5-year DPhil studentship studying how tree root systems resist vertical, horizontal and moment loading, to develop low-carbon biomimetic foundation systems for rail, energy and building applications.
title: Research Studentship in Geotechnical Engineering: Nature-based and biomimetic foundation systems

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship developing low-carbon cementitious repair materials (grouts, mortars and concrete) to extend the life of existing concrete infrastructure.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with M Group: Low whole life carbon cementitious repair materials for future infrastructure

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship developing low-carbon, crack-resistant concrete mixes with sustainable fibres and additives for precast shaft and tunnel segments.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with Tracey Concrete: Next generation low-carbon crack-resistant precast shaft and tunnel segments

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship using Network Rail data to identify climate-driven tipping points for rail assets and support long-term adaptation planning.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with Network Rail: Infrastructure system management in a changing climate

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship testing low-carbon cement binders for lower-risk rail concrete applications such as walkways, drainage channels and slope stabilisation.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with Network Rail: Low-carbon cements for low-risk rail infrastructure applications

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship using centrifuge experiments to study how railway cuttings in contrasting geological layers move under changing rainfall and dry periods.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with Network Rail: Performance of railway cuttings in geologically contrasting layers

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship combining Network Rail slope-failure data with centrifuge and finite-element modelling to identify rainfall-driven failure hotspots.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT PhD studentship with Network Rail: Understanding rainfall-induced slope failure risk

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship studying how extreme weather during placement and in service affects lower-carbon concretes used on the strategic road network.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT Studentship with National Highways: Extreme weather implications for concrete behaviour

department: Department of Engineering
summary: A four-year MRes+PhD studentship de-risking the adoption of lower-carbon concretes with high cement replacement, testing durability and service-life performance.
title: EPSRC FIBE3 CDT Studentship with National Highways: Rapid, low risk, adoption of lower carbon concrete

department: Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering
summary: A UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award collaborative PhD with Vale investigating tailings behaviour, liquefaction and dam stability, with lab testing, field monitoring and numerical modelling.
title: De-risking and De-construction of Tailing Dams

department: Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering
summary: A UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award collaborative PhD with AXA XL and the Global Earthquake Model using machine learning and geospatial data to improve multi-hazard vulnerability models for buildings.
title: Enhancing Exposure and Vulnerability Modelling for Multi-hazard Risk Using Machine Learning and Multi-Source Damage Data

department: Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering
summary: A UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award collaborative PhD with Aon Impact Forecasting developing vulnerability functions linking landslide intensity to bridge damage and economic loss, with a placement at Aon.
title: Vulnerability Modelling of Bridge Infrastructure Subjected to Landslide Hazards

department: Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering
summary: A UCL EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award collaborative PhD with Taylor Woodrow modelling how construction errors spread through a project and where intervention pays off most, with a placement at HS2 Old Oak Common.
title: Getting It Right First Time: from Construction Error Propagation to Targeted Intervention and Improved Productivity

department: Department of Civil Engineering and Management
summary: A School of Engineering PhD Scholarship using robotics, AI, sensing and digital twins to enable selective building deconstruction and reuse of construction components.
title: RoboCirc: Robotic-Enabled Deconstruction and Material Passporting for Circular Construction

department: Department of Civil Engineering and Management
summary: A School of Engineering PhD Scholarship studying how key infrastructure components fail under extreme hydrodynamic loading, to inform design and retrofit for future hazards.
title: Modelling structural failure of infrastructure under extreme hydrodynamic loading

department: Department of Civil Engineering and Management
summary: A School of Engineering PhD Scholarship modelling soil liquefaction during earthquakes, a major cause of infrastructure damage, using a mesh-free method.
title: Predicting The Onset and Progression of Soil Liquefaction Using A Mesh-Free Method

department: Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
summary: A School of Engineering PhD Scholarship developing mechanistic models to predict concrete behaviour at high temperatures for buildings, energy facilities and infrastructure.
title: Discovering Mechanistic Models for Concrete at High Temperatures

department: James Watt School of Engineering
summary: A 3.5-year PhD developing a micromechanics-based constitutive model for granular materials, applied to cyclic liquefaction of foundations and wind turbine foundations.
title: Development of a micromechanics-based constitutive theory for granular materials: from micro to macro

summary: A fully funded 3.5-year PhD investigating how changing grain shape affects wear and stress transfer in soil-structure interaction, relevant to wind turbine foundations and underground pipelines.
title: Micromechanics of grain-interface interactions (soil-structure interaction)

department: Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences
summary: A PhD linking concrete composition, mechanical properties and structural design with machine learning to cut embodied carbon while meeting engineering requirements.
title: AI for low-carbon concrete materials and structural design

department: Faculty of Engineering and Physical Sciences
summary: A PhD developing AI-assisted models to predict the durability of sustainable low-carbon concrete in marine environments, for coastal defences, ports and floating wind platforms.
title: AI-Driven Durability Design of Sustainable Concrete for Marine Infrastructure

department: School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering
summary: An EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award PhD applying causal machine learning to structural health monitoring across engineering populations, including offshore wind farms and networks of bridges.

department: School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering
summary: An EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award PhD with LimitState developing AI-enabled optimisation methods for sustainable and resilient building design, building on the Peregrine optimisation tool.
title: AI-Enabled Optimisation for the Next Generation of Sustainable and Resilient Building Design (in collaboration with LimitState Ltd.) (C3.5-MAC-He)

department: School of Mechanical, Aerospace and Civil Engineering
summary: An EPSRC Doctoral Landscape Award PhD with OFR Consultants studying how mass timber compartment fires push flames and hot gases outwards and spread fire up the outside of a building.
title: External fire spread modelling from mass timber compartment fires (in collaboration with OFR Consultants) (C3.5-MAC-McLaggan)
